title: Two complete norms that compare are equivalent
promptMarkdown:
Let $V$ be a vector space carrying two norms $\|\cdot\|_a$ and $\|\cdot\|_b$, and suppose $V$ is complete with respect to **both**. Suppose also that there is $C>0$ with $\|v\|_a\le C\|v\|_b$ for all $v\in V$.

1. Prove that the two norms are equivalent, i.e. there is also $c>0$ with $\|v\|_b\le c\|v\|_a$ for all $v$.
2. State precisely which theorem you used and check each of its hypotheses.
3. Show by example that the conclusion can fail if completeness in one of the norms is dropped. (Unit 1 contains a suitable pair of norms on $C([0,1])$.)
hintLadder: Consider the identity map $I:(V,\|\cdot\|_b)\to(V,\|\cdot\|_a)$. What does the given inequality say about $I$?
$I$ is a bijection. Which theorem gives boundedness of its inverse, and what does that inequality read as?
For part 3: on $C([0,1])$, $\|f\|_1\le\|f\|_\infty$. Which of the two norms makes $C([0,1])$ complete, and which does not?
